dedupe_keys.name: sdnet2018 a concrete crack image dataset for machine learning applications

description: SDNET2018 is an annotated concrete-image dataset published by Utah State University for training, validation and benchmarking of artificial-intelligence crack-detection algorithms. The provider explicitly connects the dataset to structural health monitoring. Its labelled structural observations support training and testing crack-detection models for condition monitoring. It contains more than 56,000 cracked and uncracked subimages derived from 230 original photographs: 54 bridge-deck images, 72 wall images and 104 pavement images. The photographed bridge decks were at the university SMASH laboratory, the walls belong to Russell/Wanlass Performance Hall, and pavement photographs come from roads and sidewalks on the university campus. A 16-megapixel Nikon camera captured the original surfaces. Images were divided into 256 by 256 pixel subimages and labelled C when a crack is present and U when no crack is present. The described crack widths range from 0.06 to 25 mm; shadows, roughness, scaling, edges, holes and debris are included as visual obstructions. The landing page lists JPEG and TXT formats and an archive descriptor. Published on 17 May 2018, the dataset has a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence and a public repository landing page. Reuse charges and acquisition dates are not stated. A limitation is that pixel dimensions and the crack-width range do not establish a constant ground sampling distance or structural load capacity. No image, annotation, archive or README body was downloaded and no detection model was executed. The related CrackForest resource covers road-surface crack images; it is a separate collection and was not merged with this bridge, wall and pavement dataset.
